introduction.summary: The study quantified the responses of ground beetle taxonomic and functional trait diversity to different tree retention practices in production forests of the Pacific Northwest, USA, comparing communities in retention patches versus clear-cut areas across five treatments.

methods.summary: The study measured carabid beetle communities across different structural retention treatments within production forests in the PNW, sampling in 2017 and 2018. The study measured the functional niche of several beetle species by quantifying morphometric traits related to their food resources (body length, mandible length, width between mandibles at their base) and dispersal ability (rear leg length and wing type).
